> @itinance Thanks. So a few things here:
> 
> 1. `pg_dump` is not a backup utility (more on this in a second) - for true backup/restore you'll want to use something like `pg_basebackup` or a utility like pgBackRest (there are a variety of tools available here). Effectively these tools take a snapshot of the binary representation of your data, so you can restore it to a similar physical environment. They'll be much more efficient than `pg_dump`/`pg_restore`, which is just recreating the SQL commands used to build your environment.
>
